# orca auth

Every `orca auth` command. Ids: a full id, a unique prefix, or (projects) a name or path.

## `orca auth login [--no-browser]`

store a person token for this terminal: an owner approves its code in the browser where they are signed in; used only with --as-person

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--no-browser`: print the code and URL only; do not open a browser (also the case over SSH on macOS and on Linux without a display)
- Exit codes: 2 the panel refused, the request was denied or expired, or its URL was not a loopback URL; 130 interrupted; the request was cancelled.

```
orca auth login
orca auth login --no-browser
orca usage set-cap --scope all --period week --tokens 500000 --as-person
```

## `orca auth logout`

revoke the stored person token and remove it (the same as orca logout)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).

```
orca auth logout
```

## `orca auth status`

the stored person token's account and expiry (never the token)

- What it does: runs locally.
- Who may: anyone; runs here, needs no panel.

```
orca auth status
```
